summary: Set up centralized log forwarding: node2 runs an 'inventory' systemd service logging via syslog tag 'inventory'; rsyslog on node2 forwards those messages over TCP/514 (with a disk-assisted, infinite-retry queue) to node1, where rsyslog (imtcp) writes them to /var/log/inventory/node2.log. Firewalld on node1 permanently allows 514/tcp. Both rsyslog and inventory.service are enabled at boot. Verified end-to-end delivery before and after independently restarting node1 and node2 (native systemctl reboot, one at a time), confirming changed boot_id and full recovery of forwarding on each.
actions_performed: Surveyed both nodes (OS, existing services, firewall, SELinux) to find no pre-existing inventory app
Created /usr/local/bin/inventory-app.sh and inventory.service on node2 to generate syslog-tagged 'inventory' log messages every 10s, enabled at boot
Created /etc/rsyslog.d/inventory-forward.conf on node2 forwarding programname=inventory messages via omfwd TCP to node1:514 with a persistent disk-assisted queue for reliability across outages
Created /var/log/inventory dir and /etc/rsyslog.d/inventory-receive.conf on node1 (imtcp on 514) writing matched messages to /var/log/inventory/node2.log
Opened 514/tcp permanently in firewalld on node1
Fixed SELinux tmp_t mislabeling (via restorecon) on the moved service unit, script, and rsyslog config files that was silently blocking service exec and rsyslog config reads (AVC denials)
Verified live log flow node2 -> node1 file with test messages
Captured baseline boot_id/service state on both nodes, then restarted node1 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id and resumed log delivery
Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id and resumed log generation + delivery to node1
